prompts: We're starting a hand-written Python support agent on Weave's multi-tenant cloud. I need three connected pieces: inspect its multi-turn conversations and tool calls, rerun a fixed set of regression questions when we change it, and send completed live answers to our own HTTP policy-scoring endpoint. Give me a compact setup outline. What remote-scoring prerequisites must be in place before Weave can call that endpoint, and does that scoring finish before the user receives the answer?

**Short answer:** Use Weave's Agents tracing to inspect conversations, `EvaluationLogger` for regression reruns, and a remote scorer signal for your endpoint. Before Weave can call your endpoint, remote scoring must be enabled for your organization, and the endpoint's host must be on an allowlist. The documentation describes scoring as a separate step that starts after the turn ends. It doesn't state a latency guarantee for the user's response.

**Setup outline**

1. **Inspect conversations and tool calls.**
   - Run `pip install weave`, then call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` call [S7].
   - Without `weave.init()`, these tracing functions silently do nothing [S7].
   - The data model covers conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool executions. The **Agents** tab shows each conversation as a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls [S3].

2. **Rerun regression questions.**
   - The agent-evaluation tutorial uses `weave.EvaluationLogger` with a `dataset` name and a `model` label. After you change the agent, you rerun the same tasks with a new label such as `"v2"` [S9].
   - Weave's compare-evaluations feature then shows whether the new version improved or regressed on your logged scores, latency and cost [S9].

3. **Send completed answers to your HTTP endpoint.**
   - Create a remote scorer signal. It is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, created in the UI or with the SDK [S2].
   - In the SDK, you publish a `RemoteScorer` and then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` [S11].
   - Weave scores only completed turns. It does not score individual LLM or tool spans, or whole conversations [S2].

**Prerequisites for remote scoring on multi-tenant cloud**

- An organization or billing admin must open the organization's Forge settings, go to the **Remote scoring** tab, and turn on **Enable remote scoring**. Remote scoring is off until this is done [S5].
- The admin must add each host that scorers may call under **Allowed hosts**. Saving requires at least one host [S5].
- If no allowlist exists, the worker rejects every host. It also rejects loopback, private, internal and cloud-metadata addresses [S5].
- HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP. Redirects aren't followed [S5].
- Choose an authentication mode, `static_bearer` or `oauth_client_credentials` [S6].
- Store the token or client secret in the secret store of the team that owns the project, before you register the scorer. The `RemoteScorer` holds only the secret name [S6].
- Your endpoint must accept a JSON `POST` and return a JSON score [S10]. Turn scoring needs the structured result format, because Weave stores tags and ratings as typed feedback columns [S2]. I did not read the exact request and response schema. Read the "Request" and "Response" sections of that page before you build the endpoint.

**Does scoring finish before the user gets the answer?**

The documentation doesn't answer this directly. It describes this sequence:
- A turn ends and Weave emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`.
- A separate agent scoring worker then sends the `POST`.
- The worker writes the result as feedback on the turn [S2].

So scoring is triggered by a completed turn, after the answer exists. Nothing I read says your agent's reply waits for the score. I can't confirm a timing guarantee from the searched snapshot.

Plan for these retry and timeout rules:
- The worker retries `5xx`, `408` and `429` responses with the same `Idempotency-Key`. It makes up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first [S2].
- A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds and isn't retried [S2].
- If your endpoint can't score in time, return `503` quickly so Weave retries [S2].

**Next step:** Ask your admin to enable remote scoring and allowlist your scoring host. Then store the bearer secret in the team secret store and register the `RemoteScorer`.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

## Organize and compare evaluations

You improve an agent by changing its application and checking whether the change helped. The system prompt, the tools, the control flow, and the underlying LLM are all considered part of the model version. To compare two versions, run the evaluation again on the changed agent, labeled as a new version.

Re-run with a different `model` label:

```python lines highlight="4" theme={"system"}
# v2: the same tasks and loop, running a changed agent (e.g. a revised system prompt).
ev = weave.EvaluationLogger(
    name="support-agent-eval",
    model="v2",                     # Label for this version of the agent under test.
    dataset="support-refund-tasks",
)
# ... same loop as v1, running the changed agent ...
```

Weave lets you [Compare evaluations](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/compare_evals.md), so you can see whether v2 improved or regressed against v1 on the scores you logged, plus latency and cost.

sources.heading: How agent turn scoring works
sources.text:
## How agent turn scoring works

An agent turn is scored in the following sequence:

1. A turn ends. When a root span (a span with no parent) ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits a `weave.genai.turn_ended` event.
2. The agent scoring worker loads the project's active signals that target `weave.genai.turn_ended`, then applies each signal's filters and sample rate.
3. For each `RemoteScorer` on a matching signal, the worker builds a `schema_version: 2` request from the turn's span, including its messages, resolves the scorer's credentials, checks the endpoint URL against the allowed hosts, and sends the `POST`.
4. The worker validates the response and writes the result as feedback on the turn. Tags and ratings appear on the **Signals** tab.

Weave scores only completed turns. Individual LLM and tool spans, and whole conversations, aren't remote scoring targets. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, whether you create it in the UI or with the SDK.

The worker retries a failed attempt with the same `Idempotency-Key`, up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first attempt. A `5xx`, `408`, or `429` response is retried. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds, so a timed-out request isn't retried. Any other `4xx` response isn't retried. If your endpoint can't score a turn in time, return `503` quickly rather than letting the request time out, so that Weave retries it. Agent turn scoring requires the structured result format, because Weave stores the tags and ratings as typed feedback columns.

### Python SDK

Publish a `RemoteScorer`, then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` and targets `weave.genai.turn_ended` in `op_names`.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.flow.monitor import Monitor
from weave.scorers.remote_scorer import RemoteScorer, StaticBearerAuthConfig

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

scorer = RemoteScorer(
    name="policy_remote_scorer",
    endpoint_url="https://scoring.example.com/weave/score",
    config={"threshold": 0.9},  # Sent to your endpoint as scorer.config
    auth_config=StaticBearerAuthConfig(
        mode="static_bearer",
        bearer_secret_name="WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORER_BEARER_TOKEN",
    ),
)
weave.publish(scorer, name="policy_remote_scorer")

monitor = Monitor(
    name="policy_remote_signal",
    scorers=[scorer],
    op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"],  # Score completed agent turns
    sampling_rate=1.0,
)
```

sources.text:
## Enable remote scoring

Remote scoring is off until it's enabled for your organization or deployment, and the scoring worker calls a scorer endpoint only if its host is on an allowlist. How you enable it depends on your deployment type.

**Multi-tenant Cloud**

To enable remote scorers for an organization, an organization or billing admin must:

1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/account-settings/[ORGANIZATION]/settings`, replacing `[ORGANIZATION]` with the organization that owns your project.
2. Select the **Remote scoring** tab.
3. Turn on **Enable remote scoring**.
4. Under **Allowed hosts**, click **Add host** and enter each host that remote scorers may call. Saving with remote scoring enabled requires at least one host. Leave the port blank to allow any port on that host.
5. Click **Save settings**.

**Dedicated Cloud**

Ask Forge to enable remote scoring for your deployment and configure its allowed hosts.

**Self-Managed**

If you run Weave in a [W\&B Self-Managed](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/self-managed.md) deployment, set these environment variables through `extraEnv` on each scoring worker: the online evaluation worker, the call scoring worker, and the agent scoring worker.

| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORING_ENABLED` | `false` | Turns on outbound requests to remote scorers. When `false`, no remote scorer runs, regardless of other settings. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Timeout for each request to a scorer endpoint. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | empty | Comma-separated operator allowlist of `host` or `host:port` entries. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_VALIDATE_HOSTS` | `true` | Enforces the allowed hosts lists. Private, loopback, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected regardless of this setting. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | `false` | Permits `http://` endpoint URLs. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` | empty | Comma-separated CIDR networks, such as `10.0.0.0/8`, whose private addresses remote scorers may call. |

To show the remote scoring settings and scorer options in the Weave UI, also set `GORILLA_GATE_WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORING=true` on the W\&B server.

**Allowed host rules**

The scoring worker checks every scorer endpoint URL, and separately the OAuth token endpoint URL when a scorer uses OAuth, against these rules:

* An entry matches an exact host, with an optional port. An entry without a port allows any port on that host.
* An entry that starts with `*.` matches subdomains at any depth, but not the domain itself. `*.corp.example.com` matches `a.corp.example.com` and `a.b.corp.example.com`, not `corp.example.com`. The suffix after `*.` must contain at least two labels, so `*.com` is rejected. A wildcard can't be combined with an IP address.
* When both an operator allowlist and an organization allowlist exist, the URL must satisfy both. An empty operator allowlist adds no restriction. When no allowlist exists at all, the worker rejects every host.
* Loopback, private, internal, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected. On Self-Managed, private addresses in the networks listed in `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` are allowed.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

### Python SDK

Publish a `RemoteScorer`, then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` and targets `weave.genai.turn_ended` in `op_names`.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.flow.monitor import Monitor
from weave.scorers.remote_scorer import RemoteScorer, StaticBearerAuthConfig

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

scorer = RemoteScorer(
    name="policy_remote_scorer",
    endpoint_url="https://scoring.example.com/weave/score",
    config={"threshold": 0.9},  # Sent to your endpoint as scorer.config
    auth_config=StaticBearerAuthConfig(
        mode="static_bearer",
        bearer_secret_name="WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORER_BEARER_TOKEN",
    ),
)
weave.publish(scorer, name="policy_remote_scorer")

monitor = Monitor(
    name="policy_remote_signal",
    scorers=[scorer],
    op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"],  # Score completed agent turns
    sampling_rate=1.0,
)
monitor.activate()
```

## Row digests

Beyond the raw data each endpoint returns, the response from `eval_results/query` includes an additional identifier that helps you correlate rows across runs. Each result row from the `eval_results/query` endpoint includes a `row_digest`, a content hash that uniquely identifies a specific input in the evaluation dataset based on its contents, not its position. Row digests are useful for:

* **Cross-evaluation comparison**: When you run two different models against the same dataset, rows with the same digest represent the same input. You can join on `row_digest` to compare how different models performed on the exact same task.
* **Deduplication**: If the same task appears in multiple evaluation suites, the digest lets you identify it.
* **Reproducibility**: The digest is content-addressable, so if someone modifies a dataset row (changes the instruction text, rubric, or other fields), it gets a new digest. You can verify whether two evaluation runs used identical inputs or different versions.

## How it works

The server uses the trace's ID and [deterministic hash-based sampling](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/sampling/) to decide which traces to drop and keep. If a trace contains several calls that have the same `trace_id`, the server's verdict to keep or drop a trace extends to any nested calls or spans that share the same trace ID. result.heading: How agent turn scoring works
result.text:
## How agent turn scoring works

An agent turn is scored in the following sequence:

1. A turn ends. When a root span (a span with no parent) ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits a `weave.genai.turn_ended` event.
2. The agent scoring worker loads the project's active signals that target `weave.genai.turn_ended`, then applies each signal's filters and sample rate.
3. For each `RemoteScorer` on a matching signal, the worker builds a `schema_version: 2` request from the turn's span, including its messages, resolves the scorer's credentials, checks the endpoint URL against the allowed hosts, and sends the `POST`.
4. The worker validates the response and writes the result as feedback on the turn. Tags and ratings appear on the **Signals** tab.

Weave scores only completed turns. Individual LLM and tool spans, and whole conversations, aren't remote scoring targets. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, whether you create it in the UI or with the SDK.

The worker retries a failed attempt with the same `Idempotency-Key`, up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first attempt. A `5xx`, `408`, or `429` response is retried. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds, so a timed-out request isn't retried. Any other `4xx` response isn't retried. If your endpoint can't score a turn in time, return `503` quickly rather than letting the request time out, so that Weave retries it. Agent turn scoring requires the structured result format, because Weave stores the tags and ratings as typed feedback columns.

result.text:
## Enable remote scoring

Remote scoring is off until it's enabled for your organization or deployment, and the scoring worker calls a scorer endpoint only if its host is on an allowlist. How you enable it depends on your deployment type.

**Multi-tenant Cloud**

To enable remote scorers for an organization, an organization or billing admin must:

1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/account-settings/[ORGANIZATION]/settings`, replacing `[ORGANIZATION]` with the organization that owns your project.
2. Select the **Remote scoring** tab.
3. Turn on **Enable remote scoring**.
4. Under **Allowed hosts**, click **Add host** and enter each host that remote scorers may call. Saving with remote scoring enabled requires at least one host. Leave the port blank to allow any port on that host.
5. Click **Save settings**.

**Dedicated Cloud**

Ask Forge to enable remote scoring for your deployment and configure its allowed hosts.

**Self-Managed**

If you run Weave in a [W\&B Self-Managed](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/self-managed.md) deployment, set these environment variables through `extraEnv` on each scoring worker: the online evaluation worker, the call scoring worker, and the agent scoring worker.

| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORING_ENABLED` | `false` | Turns on outbound requests to remote scorers. When `false`, no remote scorer runs, regardless of other settings. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Timeout for each request to a scorer endpoint. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | empty | Comma-separated operator allowlist of `host` or `host:port` entries. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_VALIDATE_HOSTS` | `true` | Enforces the allowed hosts lists. Private, loopback, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected regardless of this setting. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | `false` | Permits `http://` endpoint URLs. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` | empty | Comma-separated CIDR networks, such as `10.0.0.0/8`, whose private addresses remote scorers may call. |

To show the remote scoring settings and scorer options in the Weave UI, also set `GORILLA_GATE_WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORING=true` on the W\&B server.

**Allowed host rules**

The scoring worker checks every scorer endpoint URL, and separately the OAuth token endpoint URL when a scorer uses OAuth, against these rules:

* An entry matches an exact host, with an optional port. An entry without a port allows any port on that host.
* An entry that starts with `*.` matches subdomains at any depth, but not the domain itself. `*.corp.example.com` matches `a.corp.example.com` and `a.b.corp.example.com`, not `corp.example.com`. The suffix after `*.` must contain at least two labels, so `*.com` is rejected. A wildcard can't be combined with an IP address.
* When both an operator allowlist and an organization allowlist exist, the URL must satisfy both. An empty operator allowlist adds no restriction. When no allowlist exists at all, the worker rejects every host.
* Loopback, private, internal, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected. On Self-Managed, private addresses in the networks listed in `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` are allowed.
* HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP.
* Redirects aren't followed.

result.text:
## Authenticate requests from Weave

Weave authenticates to your endpoint with a bearer token. The request carries no Forge credential. The token proves to your endpoint that the request came from Weave, not the reverse. Each `RemoteScorer` uses one of two modes:

| Mode | What Weave does | What you configure |
| - | - | - |
| `oauth_client_credentials` | Requests a token from your OAuth token endpoint with the client credentials grant, sending the client ID and secret with HTTP Basic authentication (`client_secret_basic`), then sends that token to your scorer endpoint. | The token endpoint URL, the client ID, the name of the secret that holds the client secret, and an optional scope. |
| `static_bearer` | Sends a fixed token to your scorer endpoint. | The name of the secret that holds the token. |

Store the client secret or bearer token in the secret store of the team that owns the project before you register the scorer. The `RemoteScorer` configuration holds only the secret name. The scoring worker resolves the value at scoring time.

You improve an agent by changing its application and checking whether the change helped. ### Python SDK

Publish a `RemoteScorer`, then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` and targets `weave.genai.turn_ended` in `op_names`.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.flow.monitor import Monitor
from weave.scorers.remote_scorer import RemoteScorer, StaticBearerAuthConfig

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

scorer = RemoteScorer(
    name="policy_remote_scorer",
    endpoint_url="https://scoring.example.com/weave/score",
    config={"threshold": 0.9},  # Sent to your endpoint as scorer.config
    auth_config=StaticBearerAuthConfig(
        mode="static_bearer",
        bearer_secret_name="WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORER_BEARER_TOKEN",
    ),
)
weave.publish(scorer, name="policy_remote_scorer")

monitor = Monitor(
    name="policy_remote_signal",
    scorers=[scorer],
    op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"],  # Score completed agent turns
    sampling_rate=1.0,
)
monitor.activate()
```

Before Weave can call your endpoint, remote scoring must be enabled for your organization, and the endpoint's host must be on an allowlist. The documentation describes scoring as a separate step that starts after the turn ends. It doesn't state a latency guarantee for the user's response.

**Setup outline**

1. **Inspect conversations and tool calls.**
   - Run `pip install weave`, then call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` call [S7].
   - Without `weave.init()`, these tracing functions silently do nothing [S7].
   - The data model covers conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool executions. The **Agents** tab shows each conversation as a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls [S3].

2. **Rerun regression questions.**
   - The agent-evaluation tutorial uses `weave.EvaluationLogger` with a `dataset` name and a `model` label. After you change the agent, you rerun the same tasks with a new label such as `"v2"` [S9].
   - Weave's compare-evaluations feature then shows whether the new version improved or regressed on your logged scores, latency and cost [S9].

3. **Send completed answers to your HTTP endpoint.**
   - Create a remote scorer signal. It is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, created in the UI or with the SDK [S2].
   - In the SDK, you publish a `RemoteScorer` and then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` [S11].
   - Weave scores only completed turns. It does not score individual LLM or tool spans, or whole conversations [S2].

**Prerequisites for remote scoring on multi-tenant cloud**

- An organization or billing admin must open the organization's Forge settings, go to the **Remote scoring** tab, and turn on **Enable remote scoring**. Remote scoring is off until this is done [S5].
- The admin must add each host that scorers may call under **Allowed hosts**. Saving requires at least one host [S5].

- HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP. Redirects aren't followed [S5].
- Choose an authentication mode, `static_bearer` or `oauth_client_credentials` [S6].
- Store the token or client secret in the secret store of the team that owns the project, before you register the scorer. The `RemoteScorer` holds only the secret name [S6].

**Does scoring finish before the user gets the answer?**

The documentation doesn't answer this directly. It describes this sequence:
- A turn ends and Weave emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`.
- A separate agent scoring worker then sends the `POST`.
- The worker writes the result as feedback on the turn [S2].

So scoring is triggered by a completed turn, after the answer exists. Nothing I read says your agent's reply waits for the score. I can't confirm a timing guarantee from the searched snapshot.

- The worker retries `5xx`, `408` and `429` responses with the same `Idempotency-Key`. It makes up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first [S2].

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

## Organize and compare evaluations

You improve an agent by changing its application and checking whether the change helped. The system prompt, the tools, the control flow, and the underlying LLM are all considered part of the model version. To compare two versions, run the evaluation again on the changed agent, labeled as a new version.

Re-run with a different `model` label:

```python lines highlight="4" theme={"system"}
# v2: the same tasks and loop, running a changed agent (e.g. a revised system prompt).
ev = weave.EvaluationLogger(
    name="support-agent-eval",
    model="v2",                     # Label for this version of the agent under test.
    dataset="support-refund-tasks",
)
# ... same loop as v1, running the changed agent ...
```

Weave lets you [Compare evaluations](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/compare_evals.md), so you can see whether v2 improved or regressed against v1 on the scores you logged, plus latency and cost.

sources.heading: How agent turn scoring works
sources.text:
## How agent turn scoring works

An agent turn is scored in the following sequence:

1. A turn ends. When a root span (a span with no parent) ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits a `weave.genai.turn_ended` event.
2. The agent scoring worker loads the project's active signals that target `weave.genai.turn_ended`, then applies each signal's filters and sample rate.
3. For each `RemoteScorer` on a matching signal, the worker builds a `schema_version: 2` request from the turn's span, including its messages, resolves the scorer's credentials, checks the endpoint URL against the allowed hosts, and sends the `POST`.
4. The worker validates the response and writes the result as feedback on the turn. Tags and ratings appear on the **Signals** tab.

Weave scores only completed turns. Individual LLM and tool spans, and whole conversations, aren't remote scoring targets. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, whether you create it in the UI or with the SDK.

The worker retries a failed attempt with the same `Idempotency-Key`, up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first attempt. A `5xx`, `408`, or `429` response is retried. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds, so a timed-out request isn't retried. Any other `4xx` response isn't retried. If your endpoint can't score a turn in time, return `503` quickly rather than letting the request time out, so that Weave retries it. Agent turn scoring requires the structured result format, because Weave stores the tags and ratings as typed feedback columns.

sources.heading: Python SDK
sources.text:
### Python SDK

Publish a `RemoteScorer`, then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` and targets `weave.genai.turn_ended` in `op_names`.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.flow.monitor import Monitor
from weave.scorers.remote_scorer import RemoteScorer, StaticBearerAuthConfig

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

scorer = RemoteScorer(
    name="policy_remote_scorer",
    endpoint_url="https://scoring.example.com/weave/score",
    config={"threshold": 0.9},  # Sent to your endpoint as scorer.config
    auth_config=StaticBearerAuthConfig(
        mode="static_bearer",
        bearer_secret_name="WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORER_BEARER_TOKEN",
    ),
)
weave.publish(scorer, name="policy_remote_scorer")

monitor = Monitor(
    name="policy_remote_signal",
    scorers=[scorer],
    op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"],  # Score completed agent turns
    sampling_rate=1.0,
)
monitor.activate()
```

For OAuth client credentials, pass an `OAuthClientCredentialsConfig` as `auth_config` instead.

sources.text:
## Enable remote scoring

Remote scoring is off until it's enabled for your organization or deployment, and the scoring worker calls a scorer endpoint only if its host is on an allowlist. How you enable it depends on your deployment type.

**Multi-tenant Cloud**

To enable remote scorers for an organization, an organization or billing admin must:

1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/account-settings/[ORGANIZATION]/settings`, replacing `[ORGANIZATION]` with the organization that owns your project.
2. Select the **Remote scoring** tab.
3. Turn on **Enable remote scoring**.
4. Under **Allowed hosts**, click **Add host** and enter each host that remote scorers may call. Saving with remote scoring enabled requires at least one host. Leave the port blank to allow any port on that host.
5. Click **Save settings**.

**Dedicated Cloud**

Ask Forge to enable remote scoring for your deployment and configure its allowed hosts.

**Self-Managed**

If you run Weave in a [W\&B Self-Managed](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/self-managed.md) deployment, set these environment variables through `extraEnv` on each scoring worker: the online evaluation worker, the call scoring worker, and the agent scoring worker.

| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORING_ENABLED` | `false` | Turns on outbound requests to remote scorers. When `false`, no remote scorer runs, regardless of other settings. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Timeout for each request to a scorer endpoint. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | empty | Comma-separated operator allowlist of `host` or `host:port` entries. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_VALIDATE_HOSTS` | `true` | Enforces the allowed hosts lists. Private, loopback, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected regardless of this setting. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | `false` | Permits `http://` endpoint URLs. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` | empty | Comma-separated CIDR networks, such as `10.0.0.0/8`, whose private addresses remote scorers may call. |

To show the remote scoring settings and scorer options in the Weave UI, also set `GORILLA_GATE_WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORING=true` on the W\&B server.

**Allowed host rules**

The scoring worker checks every scorer endpoint URL, and separately the OAuth token endpoint URL when a scorer uses OAuth, against these rules:

* An entry matches an exact host, with an optional port. An entry without a port allows any port on that host.
* An entry that starts with `*.` matches subdomains at any depth, but not the domain itself. `*.corp.example.com` matches `a.corp.example.com` and `a.b.corp.example.com`, not `corp.example.com`. The suffix after `*.` must contain at least two labels, so `*.com` is rejected. A wildcard can't be combined with an IP address.
* When both an operator allowlist and an organization allowlist exist, the URL must satisfy both. An empty operator allowlist adds no restriction. When no allowlist exists at all, the worker rejects every host.
* Loopback, private, internal, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected. On Self-Managed, private addresses in the networks listed in `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` are allowed.
* HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP.
* Redirects aren't followed.

sources.text:
## Authenticate requests from Weave

Weave authenticates to your endpoint with a bearer token. The request carries no Forge credential. The token proves to your endpoint that the request came from Weave, not the reverse. Each `RemoteScorer` uses one of two modes:

| Mode | What Weave does | What you configure |
| - | - | - |
| `oauth_client_credentials` | Requests a token from your OAuth token endpoint with the client credentials grant, sending the client ID and secret with HTTP Basic authentication (`client_secret_basic`), then sends that token to your scorer endpoint. | The token endpoint URL, the client ID, the name of the secret that holds the client secret, and an optional scope. |
| `static_bearer` | Sends a fixed token to your scorer endpoint. | The name of the secret that holds the token. |

Store the client secret or bearer token in the secret store of the team that owns the project before you register the scorer. The `RemoteScorer` configuration holds only the secret name. The scoring worker resolves the value at scoring time.

3. For each `RemoteScorer` on a matching signal, the worker builds a `schema_version: 2` request from the turn's span, including its messages, resolves the scorer's credentials, checks the endpoint URL against the allowed hosts, and sends the `POST`.
4. The worker validates the response and writes the result as feedback on the turn. Tags and ratings appear on the **Signals** tab.

Weave scores only completed turns. Individual LLM and tool spans, and whole conversations, aren't remote scoring targets. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, whether you create it in the UI or with the SDK.

The worker retries a failed attempt with the same `Idempotency-Key`, up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first attempt. A `5xx`, `408`, or `429` response is retried. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds, so a timed-out request isn't retried. Any other `4xx` response isn't retried. If your endpoint can't score a turn in time, return `503` quickly rather than letting the request time out, so that Weave retries it. Agent turn scoring requires the structured result format, because Weave stores the tags and ratings as typed feedback columns.

## Enable remote scoring

Remote scoring is off until it's enabled for your organization or deployment, and the scoring worker calls a scorer endpoint only if its host is on an allowlist. How you enable it depends on your deployment type.

**Multi-tenant Cloud**

To enable remote scorers for an organization, an organization or billing admin must:

1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/account-settings/[ORGANIZATION]/settings`, replacing `[ORGANIZATION]` with the organization that owns your project.
2. Select the **Remote scoring** tab.
3. Turn on **Enable remote scoring**.
4. Under **Allowed hosts**, click **Add host** and enter each host that remote scorers may call. Saving with remote scoring enabled requires at least one host. Leave the port blank to allow any port on that host.
5. Click **Save settings**.

**Dedicated Cloud**

Ask Forge to enable remote scoring for your deployment and configure its allowed hosts.

**Self-Managed**

If you run Weave in a [W\&B Self-Managed](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/self-managed.md) deployment, set these environment variables through `extraEnv` on each scoring worker: the online evaluation worker, the call scoring worker, and the agent scoring worker.

| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORING_ENABLED` | `false` | Turns on outbound requests to remote scorers. When `false`, no remote scorer runs, regardless of other settings. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Timeout for each request to a scorer endpoint. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | empty | Comma-separated operator allowlist of `host` or `host:port` entries. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_VALIDATE_HOSTS` | `true` | Enforces the allowed hosts lists. Private, loopback, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected regardless of this setting. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | `false` | Permits `http://` endpoint URLs. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` | empty | Comma-separated CIDR networks, such as `10.0.0.0/8`, whose private addresses remote scorers may call. |

To show the remote scoring settings and scorer options in the Weave UI, also set `GORILLA_GATE_WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORING=true` on the W\&B server.

**Allowed host rules**

The scoring worker checks every scorer endpoint URL, and separately the OAuth token endpoint URL when a scorer uses OAuth, against these rules:

* An entry matches an exact host, with an optional port. An entry without a port allows any port on that host.
* An entry that starts with `*.` matches subdomains at any depth, but not the domain itself. `*.corp.example.com` matches `a.corp.example.com` and `a.b.corp.example.com`, not `corp.example.com`. The suffix after `*.` must contain at least two labels, so `*.com` is rejected. A wildcard can't be combined with an IP address.
* When both an operator allowlist and an organization allowlist exist, the URL must satisfy both. An empty operator allowlist adds no restriction. When no allowlist exists at all, the worker rejects every host.
* Loopback, private, internal, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected. On Self-Managed, private addresses in the networks listed in `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` are allowed.
* HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP.
* Redirects aren't followed.

all_read_evidence.text:
## Authenticate requests from Weave

Weave authenticates to your endpoint with a bearer token. The request carries no Forge credential. The token proves to your endpoint that the request came from Weave, not the reverse. Each `RemoteScorer` uses one of two modes:

| Mode | What Weave does | What you configure |
| - | - | - |
| `oauth_client_credentials` | Requests a token from your OAuth token endpoint with the client credentials grant, sending the client ID and secret with HTTP Basic authentication (`client_secret_basic`), then sends that token to your scorer endpoint. | The token endpoint URL, the client ID, the name of the secret that holds the client secret, and an optional scope. |
| `static_bearer` | Sends a fixed token to your scorer endpoint. | The name of the secret that holds the token. |

Store the client secret or bearer token in the secret store of the team that owns the project before you register the scorer. The `RemoteScorer` configuration holds only the secret name. The scoring worker resolves the value at scoring time.

## Organize and compare evaluations

You improve an agent by changing its application and checking whether the change helped. The system prompt, the tools, the control flow, and the underlying LLM are all considered part of the model version. To compare two versions, run the evaluation again on the changed agent, labeled as a new version.

Re-run with a different `model` label:

```python lines highlight="4" theme={"system"}
# v2: the same tasks and loop, running a changed agent (e.g. a revised system prompt).
ev = weave.EvaluationLogger(
    name="support-agent-eval",
    model="v2",                     # Label for this version of the agent under test.
    dataset="support-refund-tasks",
)
# ... same loop as v1, running the changed agent ...
```

Weave lets you [Compare evaluations](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/compare_evals.md), so you can see whether v2 improved or regressed against v1 on the scores you logged, plus latency and cost.

### Python SDK

Publish a `RemoteScorer`, then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` and targets `weave.genai.turn_ended` in `op_names`.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.flow.monitor import Monitor
from weave.scorers.remote_scorer import RemoteScorer, StaticBearerAuthConfig

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

scorer = RemoteScorer(
    name="policy_remote_scorer",
    endpoint_url="https://scoring.example.com/weave/score",
    config={"threshold": 0.9},  # Sent to your endpoint as scorer.config
    auth_config=StaticBearerAuthConfig(
        mode="static_bearer",
        bearer_secret_name="WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORER_BEARER_TOKEN",
    ),
)
weave.publish(scorer, name="policy_remote_scorer")

monitor = Monitor(
    name="policy_remote_signal",
    scorers=[scorer],
    op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"],  # Score completed agent turns
    sampling_rate=1.0,
)
monitor.activate()
```

For OAuth client credentials, pass an `OAuthClientCredentialsConfig` as `auth_config` instead.

Beyond the raw data each endpoint returns, the response from `eval_results/query` includes an additional identifier that helps you correlate rows across runs. result.heading: How agent turn scoring works
result.text:
## How agent turn scoring works

An agent turn is scored in the following sequence:

1. A turn ends. When a root span (a span with no parent) ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits a `weave.genai.turn_ended` event.
2. The agent scoring worker loads the project's active signals that target `weave.genai.turn_ended`, then applies each signal's filters and sample rate.
3. For each `RemoteScorer` on a matching signal, the worker builds a `schema_version: 2` request from the turn's span, including its messages, resolves the scorer's credentials, checks the endpoint URL against the allowed hosts, and sends the `POST`.
4. The worker validates the response and writes the result as feedback on the turn. Tags and ratings appear on the **Signals** tab.

Weave scores only completed turns. Individual LLM and tool spans, and whole conversations, aren't remote scoring targets. A remote scorer signal is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, whether you create it in the UI or with the SDK.

The worker retries a failed attempt with the same `Idempotency-Key`, up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first attempt. A `5xx`, `408`, or `429` response is retried. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds, so a timed-out request isn't retried. Any other `4xx` response isn't retried. If your endpoint can't score a turn in time, return `503` quickly rather than letting the request time out, so that Weave retries it. Agent turn scoring requires the structured result format, because Weave stores the tags and ratings as typed feedback columns.

Remote scoring is off until it's enabled for your organization or deployment, and the scoring worker calls a scorer endpoint only if its host is on an allowlist. How you enable it depends on your deployment type.

**Multi-tenant Cloud**

To enable remote scorers for an organization, an organization or billing admin must:

1. Open `https://forge.coreweave.com/account-settings/[ORGANIZATION]/settings`, replacing `[ORGANIZATION]` with the organization that owns your project.
2. Select the **Remote scoring** tab.
3. Turn on **Enable remote scoring**.
4. Under **Allowed hosts**, click **Add host** and enter each host that remote scorers may call. Saving with remote scoring enabled requires at least one host. Leave the port blank to allow any port on that host.
5. Click **Save settings**.

**Dedicated Cloud**

Ask Forge to enable remote scoring for your deployment and configure its allowed hosts.

**Self-Managed**

If you run Weave in a [W\&B Self-Managed](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/platform/hosting/hosting-options/self-managed.md) deployment, set these environment variables through `extraEnv` on each scoring worker: the online evaluation worker, the call scoring worker, and the agent scoring worker.

| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORING_ENABLED` | `false` | Turns on outbound requests to remote scorers. When `false`, no remote scorer runs, regardless of other settings. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Timeout for each request to a scorer endpoint. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | empty | Comma-separated operator allowlist of `host` or `host:port` entries. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_VALIDATE_HOSTS` | `true` | Enforces the allowed hosts lists. Private, loopback, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected regardless of this setting. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | `false` | Permits `http://` endpoint URLs. |
| `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` | empty | Comma-separated CIDR networks, such as `10.0.0.0/8`, whose private addresses remote scorers may call. |

To show the remote scoring settings and scorer options in the Weave UI, also set `GORILLA_GATE_WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORING=true` on the W\&B server.

**Allowed host rules**

The scoring worker checks every scorer endpoint URL, and separately the OAuth token endpoint URL when a scorer uses OAuth, against these rules:

* An entry matches an exact host, with an optional port. An entry without a port allows any port on that host.
* An entry that starts with `*.` matches subdomains at any depth, but not the domain itself. `*.corp.example.com` matches `a.corp.example.com` and `a.b.corp.example.com`, not `corp.example.com`. The suffix after `*.` must contain at least two labels, so `*.com` is rejected. A wildcard can't be combined with an IP address.
* When both an operator allowlist and an organization allowlist exist, the URL must satisfy both. An empty operator allowlist adds no restriction. When no allowlist exists at all, the worker rejects every host.
* Loopback, private, internal, and cloud metadata addresses are rejected. On Self-Managed, private addresses in the networks listed in `WF_SCORING_WORKER_REMOTE_SCORER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_CIDRS` are allowed.
* HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP.
* Redirects aren't followed.

## Authenticate requests from Weave

Weave authenticates to your endpoint with a bearer token. The request carries no Forge credential. The token proves to your endpoint that the request came from Weave, not the reverse. Each `RemoteScorer` uses one of two modes:

| Mode | What Weave does | What you configure |
| - | - | - |
| `oauth_client_credentials` | Requests a token from your OAuth token endpoint with the client credentials grant, sending the client ID and secret with HTTP Basic authentication (`client_secret_basic`), then sends that token to your scorer endpoint. | The token endpoint URL, the client ID, the name of the secret that holds the client secret, and an optional scope. |
| `static_bearer` | Sends a fixed token to your scorer endpoint. | The name of the secret that holds the token. |

You improve an agent by changing its application and checking whether the change helped. ### Python SDK

Publish a `RemoteScorer`, then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` and targets `weave.genai.turn_ended` in `op_names`.

```python lines theme={"system"}
import weave
from weave.flow.monitor import Monitor
from weave.scorers.remote_scorer import RemoteScorer, StaticBearerAuthConfig

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

scorer = RemoteScorer(
    name="policy_remote_scorer",
    endpoint_url="https://scoring.example.com/weave/score",
    config={"threshold": 0.9},  # Sent to your endpoint as scorer.config
    auth_config=StaticBearerAuthConfig(
        mode="static_bearer",
        bearer_secret_name="WEAVE_REMOTE_SCORER_BEARER_TOKEN",
    ),
)
weave.publish(scorer, name="policy_remote_scorer")

monitor = Monitor(
    name="policy_remote_signal",
    scorers=[scorer],
    op_names=["weave.genai.turn_ended"],  # Score completed agent turns
    sampling_rate=1.0,
)
monitor.activate()
```

For OAuth client credentials, pass an `OAuthClientCredentialsConfig` as `auth_config` instead.

1. **Inspect conversations and tool calls.**
   - Run `pip install weave`, then call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` call [S7].

   - Weave's agent-evaluation tutorial uses `weave.EvaluationLogger` with a `dataset` name and a `model` label. After you change the agent, rerun the same tasks with a new label such as `"v2"` [S9].
   - Weave's compare-evaluations feature then shows whether the new version improved or regressed on your logged scores, latency and cost [S9].
   - The tutorial's multi-turn rows hold the prior conversation history plus the next user message [S4]. I read only the intro and the compare section. I did not read the full multi-turn code, so check it before copying it.

3. **Send completed answers to your HTTP endpoint.**
   - Create a remote scorer signal. It is a `Monitor` whose `op_names` is `["weave.genai.turn_ended"]`, created either in the UI or with the SDK [S2].
   - The SDK flow is to publish a `RemoteScorer` and then activate a `Monitor` that lists it in `scorers` [S11].
   - Weave scores only completed turns. It does not score individual LLM or tool spans, or whole conversations [S2].

**Prerequisites for remote scoring (multi-tenant cloud)**

- An organization or billing admin must open the organization's Forge settings, go to the **Remote scoring** tab, and turn on **Enable remote scoring**. Remote scoring is off until this is done [S5].
- The admin must add each host that scorers may call under **Allowed hosts**. Saving requires at least one host [S5].
- The worker rejects every host if no allowlist exists. It also rejects loopback, private, internal and cloud-metadata addresses [S5].
- HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP, and redirects aren't followed [S5].
- Choose an authentication mode, `static_bearer` or `oauth_client_credentials` [S6].
- Store the token or client secret in the secret store of the team that owning the project, before you register the scorer. The `RemoteScorer` holds only the secret name [S6].
- Your endpoint must accept a JSON `POST` and return a JSON score [S10]. Turn scoring needs the structured result format, because Weave stores tags and ratings as typed feedback columns [S2]. I did not read the exact request and response schema, so read the "Request" and "Response" sections of that page before you build the endpoint.

**Does scoring finish before the user gets the answer?**

The documentation doesn't say this in so many words. It describes the sequence as follows. A turn ends, Weave emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`, and a separate agent scoring worker then sends the `POST`. The worker writes the result as feedback on the turn [S2]. So scoring is triggered after the turn completes. Your agent's reply doesn't wait on that call, as far as the documentation describes, but it doesn't state a latency guarantee.

Timing behavior you should plan for:
- The worker retries `5xx`, `408` and `429` responses with the same `Idempotency-Key`. It makes up to three attempts within 30 seconds of the first. A timeout uses the whole 30 seconds and isn't retried [S2].
- If your endpoint can't score in time, return `503` quickly so Weave retries [S2].

**Next step:** Ask your admin to enable remote scoring and allowlist your scoring host. Then store the bearer secret in the team secret store and register the `RemoteScorer`.
